neighbours.label: ' large' describing broad scale or extent ('compare large brain regions', 'large areas', 'large-scale'), where a size adjective is expected; the same phrases with 'small/tiny' or no size word stay quiet.
fire: Early scans could only map large areas of the cortex.
The survey covered large parts of the northern coast.
Satellites track large regions of ocean at once.
Farmers cleared large tracts of forest for cattle.
The storm cut power to large sections of the city.
Older telescopes could only resolve large features on Mars.
The model works well for large populations.
Floods covered large swathes of farmland.
quiet: Early scans could only map tiny areas of the cortex.
The survey covered the northern coast in detail.
Satellites track small regions of ocean at once.
Farmers cleared the forest for cattle.
The storm cut power to parts of the city.
Older telescopes could only resolve bright features on Mars.
The model works well for small populations.

notes: Card: ' large' x7, ' big' x3, ' huge' (compare⟦ large⟧ brain regions; one⟦ big⟧ image); output promotes ' large', ' overall', ' bulk' and suppresses ' small', ' local', ' finer'. Exploratory probe: 'compare large brain regions' 0.48, 'one big loaf' 0.16, 'huge knife' 0.02; 'tiny' 0.02. The test keeps to 'large' for scale.
